title: Dataverse: build solutions with coding agents using the Dataverse plugin and Work IQ

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing understates published consumption charges and overstates the protection provided by Work IQ switches. Microsoft also documents an API for allowed MCP clients, and administrator opt-in is not a universal prerequisite for the coding plugin.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and following paragraph
claims.claim: No API is documented for Dataverse MCP allowed-client configuration.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /allowedmcpclients(allowedmcpclientid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... IsEnabled ... DisplayName | Is Enabled ... LogicalName | isenabled
claims.fix: Document the allowed-client Web API side: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) with body {"isenabled": false} disables that client; true enables it. Cite the allowedmcpclient entity and Web API references. Remove the blanket sentence that none of the switches has a documented API; keep any server-wide API gap separate.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the whole Work IQ MCP server availability control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server Block access Microsoft 365 admin API PowerShell. Opened manage-ai-experience-access; results also covered Agent 365 blocking and Work IQ request policies, but no equivalent Work IQ server-availability call was documented.

claims.claim: There is no documented separate plugin-wide UI or API switch for who can use the coding-agent plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse plugin coding agents enable admin switch default licensing charge capacity GitHub Copilot CLI. Opened plugin overview, coding-agents and security-governance; these describe installation, identity privileges and separate MCP authorization, not a plugin-wide switch.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse environment access and security permissions bound the signed-in developer's plugin actions.
claims.quote: The plugin doesn't replace Dataverse development tools or platform security. ... By using interactive authentication, the agent signs in as you and can't exceed your permissions.

claims.claim: Turning off the Microsoft 365 tenant setting overrides every environment's features and access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access. ... Work IQ participation settings serve a different purpose and don't prevent agentic access.
claims.fix: Limit the tenant cascade statement to the documented Copilot/Dataverse data-sharing connection. State explicitly that this audience/participation control does not block all agentic environment access, the separate Work IQ MCP server, or directly authenticated plugin tools; use the relevant MCP, App Access and Dataverse permission controls.

claims.claim: App Access Control is under Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity & access.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center. ... Select Security > Identity & access. ... Select App Access Control.

claims.claim: App Access can narrow which applications access an environment's data.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.claim: Business skills use Dataverse security roles including Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: Security role access requires users to have two roles. An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role ... Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.
claims.fix: Point this sentence to the cited Create and use business skills page's Share a business skill section, not the Sales agent enablement page, which does not mention Skill Sharing Role. Specify that role-based sharing needs both Skill Sharing Role and the role the skill is shared with.

claims.claim: The coding-agent capability universally requires administrator opt-in before anyone can use it.
claims.quote: Other tools used by the plugin, such as the Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI, authenticate directly and aren't subject to these MCP-specific controls. Their requests still require Dataverse authorization.
claims.fix: Use user-opt-in for the locally installed coding plugin and explain its existing environment/privilege prerequisites. Describe tenant consent and per-environment allowlisting as MCP-specific requirements, not a universal plugin gate. Separately report that Work IQ is on by default for eligible production environments, with the documented exceptions, rather than treating Work IQ as universally admin-opt-in.

claims.claim: The licensing model for the described plugin/MCP and Work IQ usage is not yet published.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed and explain the applicable Power Platform/Dataverse plan, separate coding-agent entitlement, Dataverse MCP Copilot Credit billing, and Work IQ API usage-based billing. Distinguish licensed Copilot Chat business-data grounding from direct API connections using understand-costs; do not present published connection-specific licensing as wholly unknown.

claims.claim: A low, indirect-cost-only rating fits the described MCP and Work IQ coding-agent workflows.
claims.quote: The search_data tool uses usage-based Copilot Credit billing rather than a fixed charge per tool call. ... All other tools, including the metadata search tool, follow the text and generative AI tools (basic) Copilot Credit rate per 10 responses.
claims.fix: Change cost to variable and name Copilot Credits in the rationale, distinguishing Dataverse MCP tool billing and direct Work IQ API consumption from separate coding-agent subscriptions and storage capacity.

claims.claim: Prepare is the appropriate action rating for this optional coding-agent development capability.
claims.quote: action: "prepare" ... Decide which environments allow coding agents ... Start in developer environments with interactive sign-in.
claims.fix: Set action to review for the optional coding-agent/plugin change: no verified source says existing development behaviour changes without a maker choosing it. Do not use the separate Work IQ default rollout to imply this plugin installs or runs automatically.

claims.claim: No Dataverse charge is published for the described use.
claims.quote: All other tools, including the metadata search tool, follow the text and generative AI tools (basic) Copilot Credit rate per 10 responses.
claims.fix: Replace 'No Dataverse charge is published' with the documented Dataverse MCP Copilot Credit billing model. Retain only the narrower observation that the plugin preview pages name no separate plugin fee, and cite the MCP billing documentation.
